excerpt: Blogger got you started, but WordPress gives you room to grow. Here is how to move your posts, images, and readers without losing your search rankings.

faqs.a: No, if you export and import properly. The Blogger backup file holds your posts, pages, and comments, and the WordPress Blogger importer reads that file directly. Always keep a copy of the backup file until you have checked the new site and are happy with it.
faqs.q: Will I lose my blog posts when moving from Blogger to WordPress?

faqs.a: It can, but only if old links break. If you set up redirects from your old Blogger URLs to the matching WordPress URLs and keep your post titles and content the same, Google can follow the move. Expect some short term fluctuation, then rankings usually settle once the new pages are indexed.
faqs.q: Will moving hurt my Google rankings?

faqs.a: No, but it is often a good time to get one. If you already use a custom domain on Blogger, you can point that same domain to your WordPress hosting. If you are on a blogspot address, moving to your own domain makes the business look more professional and gives you full control.
faqs.q: Do I need a new domain name to move to WordPress?

faqs.a: For a typical small business blog, the export and import take under an hour. Checking posts, setting up redirects, and fixing design details take longer, usually a day or two of focused work. Larger blogs with many posts and images should allow a full weekend and should not rush the checks.
faqs.q: How long does a Blogger to WordPress move take?

intro:
Blogger is a fine place to start a blog. It is free, simple, and you can publish in minutes. But at some point, most business owners hit its limits. You want a proper contact form, a booking page, better control over how your site looks, or plugins that do real work for your business. That is when WordPress starts to make sense.

The good news is that moving does not mean starting over. Your posts, pages, images, and comments can all come with you. The move takes a bit of care, mainly so your old links keep working and Google can find your content in its new home. Done in the right order, it is a weekend job, not a rebuild.
keyword: how to move from blogger to wordpress
meta: Learn how to move from Blogger to WordPress step by step, including exporting posts, setting up redirects, and keeping your search rankings safe.

body: Blogger is owned by Google, which means you play by its rules. You cannot install your own tools, you have limited control over the design, and you cannot easily turn the blog into a full business website with services pages, pricing, and lead capture forms.

WordPress, especially self hosted WordPress, puts you in charge. You choose your hosting, your theme, and your plugins. You can add a contact form, an appointment booking tool, an online shop, or a membership area later without moving again. For a business, that flexibility matters more than it does for a hobby blog.

There is also an ownership point worth thinking about. On Blogger, your content lives on someone else's platform. On WordPress with your own domain and hosting, the site is yours. If a platform changes its rules, your business website is not at risk.
sections.heading: Why Business Owners Outgrow Blogger

body: Never start a move without a backup. In Blogger, go to Settings, then scroll to the backup section and download a copy of your blog. This file holds your posts, pages, and comments. Save it somewhere safe on your computer, not only in your email.

Also make a simple list of your most important pages. Note down the URLs of your top posts, the ones that bring in traffic or enquiries. You will check these later to make sure they still work after the move. If you use a custom domain on Blogger, keep your login details for your domain provider handy too.

Finally, decide on your WordPress setup before you import anything. You need hosting and a fresh WordPress install on your domain. If you are still on a blogspot address, this is a good time to move to your own domain name as well, since it looks more professional and is easier for customers to remember.
sections.heading: Before You Start: Back Up Everything

body: Step one is the export. In your Blogger dashboard, open Settings and use the backup option to download your blog as an XML file. That file is the package WordPress will read.

Step two is the import. In your new WordPress dashboard, go to Tools, then Import, and choose Blogger. WordPress will ask you to install the Blogger importer plugin, which is free and official. Upload your XML file and let it run. Depending on how many posts you have, this can take a few minutes.

Step three is to assign authors. WordPress will ask who should own the imported posts. Assign them to your main admin user so everything sits under one account. Once the import finishes, check a few posts at random. Open them, look at the formatting, and make sure images and headings came through properly before you move on.
sections.heading: Step by Step: Export from Blogger and Import to WordPress

body: This is the step people most often skip, and it is the one that protects your traffic. If your old Blogger links stop working, visitors hit dead pages and Google drops those pages from its results over time. A redirect simply sends anyone visiting an old address to the right new address.

Set your WordPress permalink structure first, so your post URLs look clean and match your old ones as closely as possible. A common choice is to include the post name in the URL. Then set up redirects from your old Blogger URLs to the matching WordPress URLs. There are free redirect plugins that handle this, and your hosting provider can often help if you get stuck.

If you used a custom domain on Blogger, point that domain to your new WordPress hosting once the import is done and checked. If you used a blogspot address, keep the old blog in place with redirects rather than deleting it straight away. Give search engines time to learn the new addresses, then review your top pages again after a few weeks.
sections.heading: Keep Your Search Rankings: Redirects and Permalinks

body: Once the content is in, work through the details. Check that images load on your most popular posts. Blogger sometimes stores images in a way that needs a quick fix after import, so do not assume every image survived until you have looked.

Comments are worth keeping too, because they show real people engaging with your business. The importer brings comments with posts, but check a post or two that you know had comments. If anything is missing, your backup file is your safety net.

Then turn to design. Pick a simple, fast theme that suits a business site, not just a personal blog. Add your main pages: services, about, and contact. Add a clear call to action on the homepage, such as a phone number or a contact form, so blog readers can actually become customers. A blog that looks good but gives no next step is a missed opportunity.
sections.heading: After the Move: Images, Comments, and Design

body: The biggest mistake is deleting the old Blogger blog on day one. Keep it until you are sure the new site works, the redirects are in place, and your top pages are indexed in their new home. Deleting early leaves you with no fallback.

Another common mistake is changing everything at once: new domain, new design, new post URLs, and new content all in the same week. If traffic dips, you will not know which change caused it. Move the content first, keep URLs as close as possible, and save the big redesign for after the move has settled.

Finally, do not forget the basics after launch. Submit your new sitemap in Google Search Console, check that your contact form actually sends you messages, and test the site on a phone. Most of your readers will visit on mobile, so a site that only looks right on a desktop is only half done.
sections.heading: Common Mistakes to Avoid

title: How to Move from Blogger to WordPress
